hostedPayment.role: Normal genuine hosted Checkout setup under a distinct completed command; no Checkout response loss was injected in this case.

outcome.setup: One normal customer creation and one normal Checkout creation; both setup steps completed on attempt one under the distinct setup UUID. Payment of that exact session then promoted exactly one private inactive whole-property dwelling.
outcome.interruption: One genuine cancel_at_period_end:true subscription POST succeeded at Stripe, then its response was deliberately discarded before the target set_cancellation checkpoint. The original target remained pending on attempt one with its saved intent and exact unsuffixed SQL-cased key.
outcome.recovery: After ordinary SQL retry eligibility, provider GETs confirmed the existing cancellation effect. Attempt two completed the original command and its one step, with exactly one recovered audit and the durable cancelAtPeriodEnd:true result and independently verified paidThrough.
outcome.retries: Exact cancel, reconcileCancellation and recoverOperation retries returned the same result without a provider write, new step, new attempt or duplicate recovery audit. Two separate GET-only refreshes preserved stable billing fields, stock and the original financial chain.
outcome.paidBoundary: The active ending state retained current management access before cleanup; paidThrough matched the paid initial invoice line and subscription item period end. The actual future boundary was not reached or advanced.
outcome.cleanup: One exact owned subscription DELETE with invoice_now:false and prorate:false canceled the sandbox subscription. The complete paid Checkout, original USD 5 invoice, payment/charge chain, both command histories and promoted private stock were retained; tenant, actor and membership were deactivated.
outcome.phaseDistinction: The saved target result correctly retains cancelAtPeriodEnd:true. Post-cleanup provider state is canceled with cancel_at_period_end:false because cleanup ended the disposable subscription immediately. These represent separate verified phases.

scopeAccepted: Normal genuine hosted sandbox Checkout setup on one fresh non-login fixture, USD 5 monthly and quantity one.
One cancellation response lost after the actual period-end cancellation effect, without an existing schedule.
Original cancellation intent/key/step recovery through the deployed service and MSSQL journal after natural SQL retry eligibility.
Current paid access and independently verified paid-through boundary before cleanup.
Exact original-operation retries, separate read-only refresh retries, one retained stock promotion and unchanged original financial graph.
Owned sandbox cleanup, retained histories, unchanged protected accounts/clocks, exact worker scope, complete serving configuration and public build/SQL health.
notAccepted: Application HTTP/UI or credential-login acceptance; the hosted Stripe payment UI is only genuine setup evidence.
Automatic-worker recovery, a whole-process crash/outage, provider idempotency-key age exhaustion or natural Checkout expiry.
Natural paid-boundary execution or actual renewal, including the future 2026-12-16 boundary.
Existing-schedule release recovery, cancellation reversal, zero-stock or other subscription-operation recovery.
Cleanup failure branches such as timeout/payment races or ambiguous DELETE responses; these were reviewed offline but were not exercised in this successful run.
Remaining cessation states and races under inventory item 1; natural seven-day grace and Evia audit remain outside R5 by owner decision.
